m: Om. Of this Shri Kilaka mantra, the seer is Shiva, the metre is anushtubh, and the deity is Shri Mahasaraswati. This direction is for its recitation as a limb of the Saptashati, in order to please the Mother of the world. Om. Salutation to Chandika. Markandeya said: Om. Salutation to him whose body is pure knowledge, who has the divine eye of the three Vedas, who is the cause of attaining the good, and who bears the half-moon.
Know that all of this is a pin even among mantras. One who is always devoted to its recitation also obtains well-being.
By this, all rites, beginning with driving away, succeed for those who praise the Goddess with devotion through a host of hymns.
Without this recitation, no mantra and no herb, nor anything else, is available to that person. With the recitation, every rite, beginning with driving away, can succeed.
All of them will succeed together. Hara removed this doubt of the world, and he set forth this whole auspicious teaching.
He also made the hymn of Chandika a secret. By merit, a person duly receives that summons.
That person too obtains well-being. Of this there is no doubt, when one is collected on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight, or on the eighth.
She is not pleased in any other way than when one gives and when one receives. In this form, the great God locked it with a pin.
Whoever removes the pin and recites this Chandi every day surely becomes a siddha, then a gana, and then a gandharva.
No lack of skill comes to that person, and fear arises nowhere. That person does not fall under an untimely death, and at death attains release.
One should begin only after knowing it. One who acts without doing so comes to harm. Therefore the wise begin this complete recitation only after they know it.
Whatever good fortune and the like is seen among women, all of that is by her grace. Therefore this recitation is auspicious.
When this hymn is recited gradually, wealth arises in full measure. Therefore one should indeed begin it.
By her grace there is sovereignty, good fortune, and health, the destruction of enemies, and the highest release. Why would people not praise her?
The person who remembers Chandika constantly, even in the heart, obtains the wish that is dear to the heart, and the Goddess always dwells in that heart.
This removal of the pin, made by the great God, is set in front. Having also made it free of the pin, the collected should recite it. Thus the Kilaka hymn of the blessed Goddess is complete.
